newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Sulzer sees net profit more than doubling.
newsitem.headline: Sulzer sees net profit more than doubling.

text.p: Net profit at Swiss technology group Sulzer AG could more than double this year to levels last seen in 1994, before a two-year slump of 58 percent, chief executive Fritz Fahrni said in a newspaper interview.
"Operationally, we have the chance again to catch up with the period before the profit decline of the last two years," Fahrni told the Swiss business weekly Cash.
Asked if profits would double this year, he said: "Doubling would not be enough. We will achieve a clear jump in profits this year."
Sulzer net profit was 82 million Swiss francs last year, down 58 percent in two years from 195 million in 1994. Most of the fall was caused by a sharp drop to 92 million in 1995.
But the group said in March it was now turning around after major restructuring, including trimming loss-making units, and after paying one-off damages in a U.S. patent suit.
The restructuring also included spinning off profitable subsidiary Sulzer Medica, which makes orthopaedic and cardiovascular equipment, and offering a quarter of its equity on the stock market.
Medica started trading this week and the IPO raised about 800 million Swiss francs for Medica's growth and acquisition program.
Fahrni told Cash he saw no reason to offer any more of Sulzer's three-quarter stake in Medica to the public.
"You should never say never. But it would be just as possible to go back to the capital markets through Sulzer Holding," he said when asked about Medica's potential future capital needs.
Fahrni said he was confident about a turnaround at the two loss-makers of the group's four industrial divisions.
"At Sulzer Infra there is a very good chance that we will break even this year," he said about the division that provides maintanance and other services for buildings and plants.
Asked about weaving machinery maker Sulzer Rueti, he said, "I am confident that we will also reach this break-even point here next year."
The other two divisions, turbine and locomotive maker Sulzer Winterthur and pump and compressor unit Sulzer Roteq, posted higher operating profits last year.
